response.title: A Picture of the School Commute
response.passage: For its current project, Class 2’s student newspaper is reporting how students travel to school. The team surveyed 120 students over two days. Most said they took the bus, while fewer students walked or rode bicycles. Several bus riders told the reporters that the afternoon buses were often crowded. The editors made a chart showing the travel methods named in the survey. They posted it near the school entrance so students could see the results. A week later, some students said the chart had made them consider sharing rides, but the team had not checked whether anyone had changed their travel habits. The reporters plan to repeat the survey next term so they can compare the results.

items.answer: It is reporting how students travel to school.
distractors: It is reporting how students spend their afternoons after school.
It is reporting how teachers choose the school bus routes.
It is reporting how students’ grades changed during the term.
items.question: What is the student newspaper mainly doing for its current project?

items.answer: They included the travel methods named in the survey.
distractors: They included the number of crowded buses recorded each afternoon.
They included the grades reported by the students who took part.
They included the rides that students had already shared that week.
items.question: What did the editors include in their chart?

items.answer: They want to compare the new results with the earlier ones.
distractors: They want to check whether the same students still ride bicycles.
They want to prove that the chart caused students to share rides.
They want to replace the bus routes before the next school term.
items.question: Why do the reporters plan to repeat the survey next term?
